variants.title: Global users, single origin
variants.context: Users in Tokyo and New York hit the same app and static assets travel from one origin region.
variants.constraint: Large assets cross an ocean each time and latency climbs.
variants.question: What pattern reduces the latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Serve static assets and media from a CDN close to users.

variants.title: Images consume most of the time
variants.context: Images and scripts dominate page load time for an international audience.
variants.constraint: The page is dynamic but the heavy assets are static.
variants.question: What should be optimized first?
variants.expectedPattern: Deliver static media from edge caches, not the origin.
wrongChoices: Keep all assets on the origin

variants.title: Recent deploy does not appear instantly
variants.context: Users still fetch old static files even after a JS asset is updated.
variants.constraint: Old CDN copies are still cached.
variants.question: What prevents stale assets on deploy?
variants.expectedPattern: Version the asset URL with a hash so the cache sees a new file and fetches it fresh.

variants.title: Game patch day
variants.context: A new game patch is downloaded worldwide and the origin becomes a bottleneck.
variants.constraint: Large artifacts are static and global, but the origin is one region.
variants.question: What is the correct delivery model?
variants.expectedPattern: Use CDN edge distribution for the patch files.
wrongChoices: Route every user to the origin

variants.title: Slow page due to cross-continental static assets
variants.context: A marketing page contains heavy images and CSS served from a single region.
variants.constraint: The dynamic application is fine, but asset delivery is slow.
variants.question: What should be moved closer to users?
variants.expectedPattern: Static media and JS/CSS into edge cache locations.
wrongChoices: Route every request to the same app

variants.title: Origin not handling burst load
variants.context: A product launch causes huge bursts of static asset requests and the origin service is saturated.
variants.constraint: Static content is failing under popular demand.
variants.question: What absorbs the pressure?
variants.expectedPattern: A CDN edge layer that caches and serves static content near the user.

variants.title: Users in Africa wait 500ms for images
variants.context: The app is in Europe and all images are served from a single origin region.
variants.constraint: The bottleneck is physical distance, not compute.
variants.question: How do you reduce the latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Use edge caches in multiple regions and serve local copies of static assets.

variants.title: Slow JS bundle in each market
variants.context: The application sends the same large JS bundle to all users across several regions.
variants.constraint: Each region fetches the same static resource from a distant origin.
variants.question: What is the right optimization?
variants.expectedPattern: Serve the bundle from a nearby CDN edge.
wrongChoices: Move the bundle into the database

variants.title: Back-to-back deployments leave stale edge copies
variants.context: A front-end app is updated every day, but some users receive old CSS files from the edge.
variants.constraint: The CDN keeps caches until they expire.
variants.question: What pattern avoids stale content confusion?
variants.expectedPattern: Versioned asset names with a content hash.

variants.title: Heavy media library
variants.context: A learning platform serves thousands of video thumbnails globally and the origin is overloaded.
variants.constraint: The heavy files are static and heavily reused.
variants.question: What system design fits best?
variants.expectedPattern: Edge caching for thumbnails and media with cache invalidation on content updates.
wrongChoices: Direct data access from the primary DB

variants.title: HTML is dynamic but CSS is not
variants.context: The homepage HTML is personalized, yet 2MB of CSS and fonts are fetched from origin on every view.
variants.constraint: Personalization applies only to HTML.
variants.question: What should the CDN cache?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache immutable CSS, fonts, and images at the edge; keep HTML at the origin or with a short edge TTL.
wrongChoices: Cache personalized HTML for all users as one object

variants.title: Range requests for video
variants.context: Users scrub through 4K videos and every byte range hits origin.
variants.constraint: The files are immutable once published.
variants.question: How should video bytes be delivered?
variants.expectedPattern: Let the CDN cache segmented or range-capable objects near viewers.
wrongChoices: Proxy every range through the app server
Store video blobs in the primary SQL node

variants.title: Cache-Control missing
variants.context: Origin sends no cache headers, so the CDN revalidates every asset on every request.
variants.constraint: Assets are static for hours.
variants.question: What header policy unlocks the edge?
variants.expectedPattern: Set Cache-Control with a TTL (and hashed filenames) so the CDN can serve without origin.
wrongChoices: Unique query strings on each page view

variants.title: Cookie-busted cache
variants.context: A session cookie is sent on image URLs, so the CDN treats each user as a unique object.
variants.constraint: Images are public and identical.
variants.question: What restores hit ratio?
variants.expectedPattern: Strip cookies from static asset requests and cache them as public objects.
wrongChoices: Move images behind login on origin

variants.title: Purge storm after a typo
variants.context: Ops purges the entire CDN after fixing one CSS typo and origin CPU spikes globally.
variants.constraint: Only one file changed.
variants.question: What is the safer invalidation pattern?
variants.expectedPattern: Purge or version only the changed object, not the whole site.
wrongChoices: Turn the CDN off for an hour

variants.title: API JSON from origin every time
variants.context: A public, slowly changing catalog API is fetched from origin by every mobile client worldwide.
variants.constraint: Responses are identical for anonymous clients for several minutes.
variants.question: Can the edge help APIs?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache cacheable GET API responses at the edge with a short TTL and proper Vary headers.
wrongChoices: POST the catalog on every refresh
Cache authenticated private carts at the shared edge
Disable HTTP caching because it is JSON

variants.title: TLS handshake from far origin
variants.context: First byte to a static site is 400ms from South America because TLS terminates only in Virginia.
variants.constraint: Content is static.
variants.question: What cuts connection latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Terminate TLS at nearby CDN PoPs and serve cached content locally.
wrongChoices: More origin app servers in Virginia only

variants.title: Error pages cached as 200
variants.context: Origin returned 500 during an outage and the CDN cached that HTML as a successful object.
variants.constraint: Users still see the error after origin recovers.
variants.question: What cache rule is missing?
variants.expectedPattern: Do not cache 5xx (or use a very short error TTL) and revalidate after origin is healthy.
wrongChoices: Purge only after the next marketing campaign
Serve the error from origin forever

variants.title: Signed URL media leak via long TTL
variants.context: Private lecture videos use signed URLs but the CDN caches them as public for 7 days.
variants.constraint: Access must remain authorized.
variants.question: How should private media be edged?
variants.expectedPattern: Cache with signed URL or token validation at the edge; do not treat private objects as public.
wrongChoices: Put video bytes in the SQL primary

variants.title: SPA index.html stuck
variants.context: index.html is cached for a week, so users keep loading an old shell that points at deleted JS chunks.
variants.constraint: Hashed JS files are fine; the HTML entry is not.
variants.question: What TTL split is correct?
variants.expectedPattern: Short TTL or no-cache on index.html; long TTL on hashed static chunks.
